stem:
When $\text{ClNO}_2$ reacts with $\text{NO}$ an equilibrium is established.

$$\text{ClNO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{NO}\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{NO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{ClNO}\text{(g)}$$

In each $\text{ClNO}_2$ molecule the nitrogen atom is bonded to the chlorine atom and bonded to each of the oxygen atoms separately.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram for the $\text{ClNO}_2$ molecule.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The reaction between $\text{ClNO}_2$ and $\text{NO}$ is first order with respect to each reactant.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Write the rate equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce the units of the rate constant, $k$, when the concentrations of both gases are measured in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ and the rate is measured in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State and explain whether or not the reaction **could** take place in a single step.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: An experiment is carried out in which the initial $[\text{ClNO}_2]$ is $2.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{mol dm}^{-3}$. A large excess of $\text{NO}$ is used. The initial rate of reaction is $1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$. The rate of the reaction is assumed to be constant for the first 0.20 seconds.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Draw a graph on the grid to show how the concentration of $\text{ClNO}_2$ varies for the first 0.20 seconds.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce the concentration of the $\text{NO}_2$ product at 0.20 seconds.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
After 20 seconds the concentration of $\text{ClNO}_2$ remains constant.

Explain this observation.
